line: I ain’t been to the hood in six years, still smokin’ Zeko
vault_lines: I ain't been to the hood in six years, still smokin' Zeko
meaning:
“Smoking ___” is a term to disrespect a dead rival member.

Isaiah “Zeko” Walker was a gang member from “051 Young Money” who was shot and killed on September 27, 2008 and was 18 at the time of his death.

051 Young Money was long rivals of Chief Keef’s former hood “O'Block” which is why members from both gangs diss each other.

line: In the streets if I was Gee Money, I woulda been killed Nino
vault_lines: In the streets if I was Gee Money, I woulda been killed Nino
meaning:
New Jack City (1991) movie reference.
Nino Brown (Wesley Snipes) is an up-and-coming drug pusher. His brother and right-hand-man, Gee Money (Allen Payne) introduces Nino to a new drug: freebased “crack” cocaine, which Gee says is cheaper to produce and more potent than regular cocaine and is taking the poor neighborhoods of New York by storm.
Nino manages to escape. That night, he confronts Gee Money for his act of betrayal. Gee accuses Nino of being egotistical, and putting himself over what they built together. Gee wants things to go back to the way they were, but Nino sees no going back, and regretfully kills him.

line: They don’t want no smoke, no cancer and no cigarettes
vault_lines: They don't want no smoke, no cancer and no cigarettes
meaning:
The term “smoke,” which is slang for killing someone with a gun, although in this case, it’s a metaphor for lyrical murder. Doowop is saying that his opps don’t want to test him.

Doowop uses the cigarette smoke as a pun, as cigarettes are known to cause cancer.

A similar line was used by Chief Keef on Morgan Tracy too.
